correctness.rationale: For n>=3 a GP rook set is either one-per-column, contained in a unique full n-simplex with a double-row column and arbitrary remaining third-row cells, or contained in one column triangle. The B simplices intersect one another only in the join core; each B intersects the core in the join of an S^0 with a nonempty simplex, so core inclusion is a homotopy equivalence. The core is a join of n three-point sets and is a wedge of 2^n spheres in dimension n-1, hence simply connected. Exactly n remaining column triangles attach along null loops, giving n additional S^2. Complete independent face enumeration and mod-two homology checks for n=3..6 agree. The integral claim rests on the all-n gluing proof rather than finite ranks.

value.rationale: This classifies a canonical infinite geometric graph-product family in complete integral homotopy, showing simultaneous exponential high-dimensional and linear low-dimensional sphere multiplicities, a split core inclusion, and the collapse of n-dimensional simplices to a wedge in lower dimensions. The new qualitative information is not captured by known face polynomials and supplies a natural structural testbed for higher-row extensions.
